Commentary.Commentary: Right then. 7 overs left in the day. How many can England snare? Can Sri Lanka see off the dying moments of the day? The 4th innings is about to begin. Interesting choice - Sam Curran to start off proceedings. Dimuth Karunaratne and Kaushal Silva are the openers. Here we go!!!

A game to forget for the Lankan bowlers. Dilruwan Perera and Herath got 2 each while Akila got a parting complimentary gift in the form of Foakes' wicket. All the bowlers struggled in the heat and also the pressure of a big lead conceded and a massive target looming took the fight out of them.

Coming to the game, it has been toying or bullying by England. They have done to Sri Lanka what the hosts do to other teams - win toss, bat first, get big lead, rub salt on the wound by batting long in the second and pile up a mountain of a target in the final innings. Keaton Jennings was the chief instructor and the rest played around him. He finished unbeaten on 146 and got good support from Ben Stokes, the 107-run stand with him changing the course of the game after Sri Lanka threatened to come back briefly. After that, it was just going through the motions.

Rangana Herath leads the Sri Lankan team. Applause all around and the old man manages a smile. The result may not go Sri Lanka's way but for now, it is Herath's moment. He has toiled and toiled hard and the only active cricketer from the 90s has bowled his final ball in competitive cricket. Not a great game for him personally, a wicket in the first innings and 2 in the second but he ends his career with 433 Test wickets, finishing in joint 8th place with Stuart Broad.

Well, that was bizarre. A ball later after Root signalled Jennings to wait, he has called his men back. Keaton Jennings stays unbeaten, on 146 and Sri Lanka have a mammoth target of 462 with a minimum of 187 overs to be bowled. 7 of those are scheduled today.

Cannot say Sri Lanka have bowled too badly. They were looking deflated but only after Stokes started to attack. They have tried everything, even negative line bowling but when a team gets a first-innings lead close to 150 on a turning Asian track, no matter what the other unit does, the former always seems to be on top. Join us back at 1500 local (0930 GMT) for the final session.

The hosts had some sort of a chance when the post-Lunch session began and started well too - with the bowlers keeping it tight and not giving away runs. But then, Ben Stokes started to counter-punch and that changed the situation. Jennings meanwhile has moved on to 98 and it is only a matter of time that England declare. May be an hour after Tea would be the choice.

England are effectively 250/3 now. The highest 4th innings total at this venue is 300 by Pakistan, that too, in a lost cause, in 2012. The highest score to save a Test match is 210/9 by England, way back in 2003. No team has chased even 100 at this venue in the 4th innings but if the Lankans manage to bowl England out in the second session, they will give themselves some sort of a chance. Please do come back at 1240 local (0710 GMT).

The plan to choke seemed to work. For the first hour, England were pretty good, losing only Burns but then suddenly lost two more in quick succession. That is what happens when the scoreboard does not move. However, with Keaton Jennings still unbeaten, the visitors have managed to ensure that there was no collapse as such.

The batsman works it down the leg side. One run added to the total.
Another defensive shot from the crease.
Comes forward and defends it well again.
Outside off, played towards point.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Dilruwan switches ends now, coming in from where Herath was bowling.
Pushes this down to long off for one more.
Full and outside off, KJ lunges to defend and the ball goes off the outside edge past first slip. A single taken.
Goes back and works it through the leg side for a run.
Full and outside off, pushed through the covers for a single.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

HUGE, HUGE SHOUT FOR LBW! Not out. No review taken. Lakmal is almost laughing at Dickwella who laughs in return. Was that bat first? Full and around off, Jennings got a good stride forward as he looked to defend and the ball seemed to hit the bat and pad at the same time. A closer look in the replays reveal that the ball hit the pad first and Hawk Eye shows it to be plumb!
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Short now, cut through cover for a couple. Stokes moves to 11 from 20 balls.
Darted this around middle and leg, Stokes is hurried into his defense on his back foot.
Full and around middle, watchfully defended.
Stop the press. Jennings finally connects properly with his reverse sweep. Full and outside off, Keaton gets it towards third man for a single.

He is definitely looking to be aggressive. Sees the length short and looks to cut, hits it uppishly but the ball lands just short of point. Might as well hold on to his horses. Just 10 minutes to go to Lunch.
Gets a long way across but then defends.
The paddle now, through fine leg for a run.
Floated around off, pushed back to the bowler.
Gets the punch right this time, past the bowler towards long off for a single.
Oops... a touch shorter than full, Stokes goes back to punch but the ball barely bounces. An inside edge results, onto the pads.
Dhananjaya de Silva replaces Akila Dananjaya.
Down the leg side, swept fine for a run.

MISFIELD FROM THE ACTING CAPTAIN. He is flat on his face. On middle, Keaton punches it down the ground. Suranga Lakmal dives from short mid-wicket but after the ball passes him. Takes a long time to get up. A single taken.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full and outside off, pushed towards cover. Ben Stokes is a long way down for the single but is sent back in time.

Oops... how did that happen? Full and outside off, Jennings looked to play the reverse sweep but as has been happening all morning, he was nowhere near the pitch of the ball. It took the bottom edge, bounced and went off the back of the bat over leg slip! Two runs taken.
Too straight, around middle and leg, clipped towards backward square leg.
Much better. Fuller and straighter, blocked out.
FOUR! TAKE THAT! Probably the worst delivery of the morning. Dragged down way too short,  Stokes rocks back and pulls it through mid-wicket for a boundary! The stand is now worth 23 from 32 balls.
On middle and leg, watchfully defended.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. One run added to the total.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Shorter in length, blocked to the off side.
FOUR LEG BYES! Pitched well outside leg, Stokes misses his sweep but the ball goes off his pads, past the keeper who is busy appealing for LBW, down to the fine leg fence. The lead is now 231.
Tossed up, around leg, pressed through mid-wicket for one.
Fuller and flatter, blocked on the back foot.
Short in length, pulled down to long on for a run.
Around middle, defended from the crease.
Full on middle and leg, flicked through mid-wicket for a single.
Very full, around off, jabbed towards point.
Full and around middle, watchfully defended.
FIFTY FOR JENNINGS! His second in Test cricket. Very, very important innings for him. Now, to kick on and get that hundred. Gets there with a gentle tickle through fine leg for a single.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Again the line is outside leg, again the paddle is attempted, again the shot is missed and again the 'AIYOOO!' is heard.
Full and outside leg, Jennings gets across and looks to paddle but misses. He has been out bowled recently around his legs, playing that shot.
Dilruwan gets a rest. Akila Dananjaya is on. Lacked a little bit of patience in the first innings.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Outside off, KJ plays it very late, behind point for a single.
Another LBW shout, not out again. Coming from around the wicket, this is pitched around leg and maybe going on too straight, as Keaton misses his defense, to be hit on the pads.

Massive shout! But not out! No review taken. Landed outside off, Jennings looks to defend but the ball spins in, goes between bat and pad and Dickwella behind makes a good collection. As expected, he is up and shouting but not sure for what. Neither is Herath sure. He thinks about the review but then lets it be. Replays show that the ball missed the inside edge and probably clipped the front pad but the impact was outside off.
On middle, helped through mid-wicket for a run.
Full and outside off, played behind point for a single.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

MISFIELD, FOUR! First boundary of the morning and it has come due to a sloppy effort. Full and outside off, Jennings drives this through the covers where Kaushal Silva is a tad lazy in getting down to his left. He misses and his opening partner, Dimuth Karunaratne, has too much of work to do from mid off. He races across the turf, gets to the ball with a dive but cannot prevent the boundary.
Beaten! Another ripper. Slower through the air and that generates purchase for Dilruwan. He lands this on a good length outside off, gets Jennings lunging and then rips it past the outside edge.
This is straighter, around middle, watchfully defended in front of short leg.
Full and outside off, left alone.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Goes back and across to tuck it through square leg for a run.
On middle and leg, flicked through the leg side for a single to get off the mark.
Ben Stokes comes in at number 5, replacing his captain.

OUT! Caught behind! Herath gets the skipper again! Who needs an end change or a field change when the bowler can bowl like that? Beautiful bowling from the 40-year old. Tosses this around off, gets Root to come forward and then makes the ball to turn away slightly to take the outside edge. Then, you need good support from your keeper as well and Dickwella takes that perfectly. Immediately leaps up in celebration and honest Root does not even wait for the umpire's finger to go up. A bad Test for Root, flopping in both innings. All of a sudden, England have slipped from 60/0 to 74/3.
Gets across and works it behind square leg for a single.
Likes that reverse sweep. Brings it out again but is not to the pitch of the ball. Gets it off the bottom edge, on the bounce, to first slip.
The arm ball, around off, Keaton gets too close to the ball and just about brings his bat down in time to cut, getting the ball through point for a single. Moves to 40.
Excellent bowling. Landed outside off, Jennings comes forward to defend but the ball spins away after landing on the rough to beat the outside edge.
Fuller on middle, pushed towards mid on.
Around off, worked through mid-wicket for a single.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full and outside leg, Root looks to sweep but misses.
UPPISH BUT SAFE! Full and outside off, Root plays this a touch loosely, pushes it in the air, through the covers but wide of the man over there. A single taken.
Fuller and around off, pushed back to the bowler.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full and around middle, Root lunges to defend but gets it off the inner half of the bat towards short leg.
That ball has taken the inside edge of the batsman and thudded into his pads.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
Russel Arnold on air reckons that Rangana Herath should switch ends. Feels that there is more turn at the end from where Dilruwan is bowling.
Stays back and defends.
Outside off, pushed towards cover.
Full and around middle, pushed towards mid off.
Goes back and with effective wristwork, flicks it through mid-wicket for a run. The skipper is off the mark.
Floated outside off, spinning in, Root goes back and defends.
A touch short outside off, punched through the covers for a single.
Full and around off, watchfully pushed out.
Thrown up with a bit more loop, around off, spinning away, Root opens the face of the bat and pushes it towards point.
Very full and tight, well blocked.
Full and around off, solidly defended back to the bowler.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.
Played to the mid-wicket region by the batsman.
Full and outside off, Root looks to sweep but misses. There is a big LBW shout but it is turned down. Impact was outside off.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Around off, Root goes back and defends.
Skipper Joe Root walks in at number 4, replacing Moeen.

OUT! Oh dear. What a waste of a wicket. We did feel that Moeen should counter-attack but that is just a poor shot. Full on middle, Moeen lazily attempts to swing across the line. Is nowhere near the pitch of the ball and he gets it off the inner half towards mid on. It is so poorly timed that it barely carries. Rangana Herath over there has to struggle to get to the ball and nearly cradles it, with the ball, luckily for him, getting stuck in his palms around his box. Please don't imagine how. He is all smiles though, taking a bit of a while to get up.
The batsman has pushed it to the cover region. One run added to the total.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.

DRINKS BREAK. Superb opening hour for England. They have lost just the wicket of Burns, that too, because of a superb piece of fielding. The pitch has already started to turn and it might be a good idea for Moeen to counter-attack.
This is slightly quicker, Moeen calmly blocks it out.
Slowly tossed up outside off, pushed back towards Herath again.
Very full outside off, almost a yorker, dug out back to the bowler.
Short and outside off, played behind point for a run.

Was there an inside edge? Dickwella almost gets excited for everything. Here come the replays. Full and around leg, Jennings gets back and looks to flick but the ball hits his pads and lobs in the air, towards the vacant short leg region.
On middle, pushed down to long on for a single. Way too easy for a new batsman.
It was a matter of time before he was brought on. Here comes Rangana Herath.
On middle, blocked in front of short leg.
Full and outside off, driven back to Dilruwan.
BEATEN! How did that miss the off stump? Full and around off, Jennings looks to defend but the ball spins just away, past the outside edge and shaves the off stump!
This is on middle, well pushed towards the bowler.
Around off, solidly defended to the off side.
On middle and leg, helped to the leg side for a single.
Full and outside off, pushed through the covers for a couple.
A short ball, down the leg side, pulled towards fine leg for a single.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Full again, pushed towards cover once more.
Fuller in length, solidly pushed towards cover.
Avoids the king pair. Lakmal had cleaned him up in the first innings and this time too, Moeen faces him first up. Sees the ball coming in from outside off on a length and blocks.
In comes Moeen Ali at number 3. He is on a king pair.

OUT! Superb piece of fielding from Dimuth Karunaratne and Burns has to go! What a way to get a breakthrough. Fuller on middle, Rory comes down the track and flicks it towards mid on. He calls for the single, there is no miscommunication and the running is pretty decent too. However, Karunaratne comes way too quickly from mid on for Burns' liking, has one stump to aim at and throws at the bowler's end. Bulls' eye! It looks out to the naked eye but the umpire wants to be sure. Refers it upstairs and replays confirm that the highest opening stand for England in the second innings, in 10 innings, has finally been broken. The last time the openers stitched a 50-run stand in the second innings was 53, by Alastair Cook and Mark Stoneman in the Ashes, at the Adelaide Oval, in December 2017.
Direct hit! Is Burns in trouble? He does not seem to be happy. Referred upstairs...
Goes back and works it through square leg for a run. The stand is now worth 60.
Full and just outside off, pushed towards cover.
Down the leg side, Rory looks to flick but misses. The ball goes off his thigh pads through fine leg. A leg bye taken.
This time hs leans and drives it towards cover.
Once again Burns is down the track, is nowhere to the pitch of the ball, looks to defend awkwardly and gets it off the outer half towards point.
Good length delivery outside off, coming in, dead-batted to the off side.
On middle and leg, helped through mid-wicket to get across to the other end.
ANOTHER NO BALL. Second from Lakmal this morning. This is for overstepping. Full and just outside off, Burns gets across, comes forward, then goes back and defends.
Back of a length this time, watchfully defended.
On a length around off, coming in, watchfully defended.
On middle and leg again, this time Rory tucks it to the left of the man at deep mid-wicket. Two more.
On middle and leg, worked through mid-wicket for a couple. Burns moves to 20.
Full and straight, blocked towards mid on.
Loose delivery, outside leg, flicked wide of mid-wicket for a quick single. Good understanding between the two openers. The running and calling has been error-free.
Short and wide, cut straight to cover.

Risky, very risky. Burns is leading a risky life at the moment. Full and in line of the stumps, Rory gets across to paddle and luckily for him, the ball hits his gloves and rolls down. That was heading for the wickets and the left-hander had got way too across.
The response is to come down the track immediately. Is nowhere near the pitch of the ball and somehow, gets bat on that, managing an under edge.

BEATEN! That spun. Guess we are going to see that regularly. Landed around the good length area, around the off stump, Burns comes forward to defend but the ball lands, generates a puff of dust and then spins past the outside edge.
In line of the stumps, coming in slightly, blocked towards point.
Outside off, pushed towards cover.
Fuller in length, just around middle, watchfully defended towards cover.
Landed around off, going away, Jennings shoulders arms.
Similar ball, pushed towards cover.
On a length around middle, defended to the off side.
Now Burns tries the reverse sweep but gets an under edge onto the pads. A happening over.
OOPS! Full on middle, KJ looks to flick now but the slow away turn induces a leading edge, wide of cover! A single is taken.

Another LBW shout, but the impact is well outside off. Keaton brings out the reverse sweep but he signals his intentions way too early. Hence, Dilruwan slows down the delivery and hits the batsman on the pads.
Full and around off, nicely pushed in front of cover for a quick single. The lead is now 190.
Similar line, this time Jennings lunges and pushes it back to the bowler.
The arm ball, around leg stump, played in front of short leg.
Flicks it through the leg side to bring up the 50-RUN OPENING STAND. This has been a good, solid start by the visitors.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

TOP EDGE, SAFE! It has been given a no ball anyways. Did Lakmal overstep? A short ball outside off, Burns looked to pull but the bounce got big on him. Went off the top edge and straight up in the air. However, there are more crows than men around the mid-wicket region close to the batsman. By the time the man from the deep comes running in, a single is taken.
An issue with the ball. The seam seems to be coming away. Marais Erasmus has a look, cuts a thread and then hands it back to Lakmal.
On a length outside off, played towards point for a run.

A well-taken single. Burns pushes this fuller length delivery towards mid off, sees that Angelo Mathews is resting on his heels, not quite attacking the ball and pounces on the opportunity. Angelo realizes late that he has been caught napping and tries to hurry, picks it up and has a shy at the bowler's end but Rory is in by that time. The stumps are missed any which ways.
Tighter line, watchfully defended.
On a length outside off, placed towards cover.
Floated around middle, RB comes down the track and drives it towards long on for one.
Outside off, punched through the covers for a run.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Good use of the feet, comes down the track and flicks it wide of mid on for a single.

NOT OUT! Saved by a hair's breadth! Marginal call, as Hawk Eye shows the impact to be umpire's call. A very good delivery from Dilruwan. After bowling the one that spun on the previous ball, he darts this one around off. Burns does not pick it and thrusts his pad forward, ahead of his bat and is pinged on the equipment. Perera appeals long and hard but umpire Gaffaney is unmoved. Dilruwan convinces Lakmal to go for the review which he does, but Hawk Eye saves the batsman. Good thing for Sri Lanka - at least they do not lose a review.
LBW review! The Lankans reckon that they have Burns plumb in front. Looks close.
Short and outside off, spinning away, Burns goes back to cut but there is slow turn, hence a bottom edge is induced.
Landed outside off, left alone.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. They pick up a single.
This is just outside off, Burns initially comes forward, but then goes back and blocks.
Around off, coming in slightly, watchfully defended.
Around off, played with an open bat-face behind point for a single. The lead is now 180.
Landed outside off, coming in, left alone.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Landed around off, watchfully defended.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Comes down the track, is not to the pitch of the ball, looks to flick but gets a thick inside edge onto his pads.
Landed outside off, Burns looks to defend but the ball spins away and beats the outside off.
One more leave outside off.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to cover.
Wider outside off, not played at again.
Closer to the off stump, coming in as well, but Keaton knows where his sticks are and lets it go.
Landed outside off, a touch wide, Jennings shoulders arms.
A length ball outside off, coming in, pushed towards mid on.
Suranga Lakmal to bowl from the other end. Dinesh Chandimal is off the field, so Lakmal is leading the pack.
On middle and leg, kept in front of short leg.
Landed outside off, short in length, slow spin away, Keaton looks to cut but the ball comes so slowly that it goes off the bottom part of the bat towards cover. A run taken.
This time he comes forward properly and defends correctly.
Similar ball, Jennings gets a good stride forward and blocks it, slightly off the inner half, towards short leg.
On middle and leg, watchfully defended.
Full and down the leg side, flicked through square leg for an easy single.

Alright then. The players are onto the field. The Lankans get into a huddle. They need to get 10 wickets ASAP. Can they bowl out England under 150? The lead is a healthy 177 as of now, but 3 or 4 wickets quickly will raise the Lankan hopes. Dilruwan Perera will start off proceedings to Rory Burns. Here we go!

PITCH REPORT - Brad Hogg observes that the pitch has started to crumble around the good length area. There are some pebbles coming out and what that might do is - just ask the bowlers to hit that area consistently. Reckons that there will be plenty of wickets to fall this afternoon and THIS GAME SHOULD END TOMORROW.

Moeen Ali has a chat with Ian Ward. The all-rounder says that the pitch is turning but one needs to be very patient. Feels that his team's seamers were fantastic early on and the spinners did their bit. Reckons that England are way ahead in the game and need to build on the advantage today. On the bowling, Moeen says that the plan was to bowl a disciplined line and length and then save the boundaries. Feels that partnerships with the bat are the key on Day 3. On his own bowling, he says that he is changing his pace as much as he can. Adds that the wicket is spinning but is very slow. So, he tried to keep it in line of the stumps and was patient, hoping that something would happen sometime. Informs that before the series, the entire bowling group sat down and laid out a plan to bowl and they have been executed petty well. On spin coach Saqlain Mushtaq, Ali is full of praise for the Pakistan legend, saying that he has got plenty of knowledge, more than any other.

WEATHER - There were some nervous moments regarding this topic. Last evening, after Stumps, there was a heavy shower and it was pretty overcast this morning. But now, the clouds have disappeared and we have bright and sunny conditions.

20 wickets in 2 days. Nothing surprising. What is surprising is - England leading by a BIG margin in Galle. Galle, yes, Galle - the one stadium which is considered to be a fortress for Sri Lanka. Patient batting and disciplined bowling, working to plans has given the visitors a big ascendancy in this game. Will the Lankans be able to fight back? Hello and a warm welcome to third day of the opening Test between Sri Lanka and England at Galle.
... DAY 3, OPENING SESSION ...

England now have a lot of time on their hands and also all their 10 wickets. They will try and bat the Lankans out of the game. Anything around 350 is going to be an uphill task for the home side. Is there a fightback in store or will England continue their domination? Join us on Day 3, at the same time to find out. Cheers!

Earlier in the day, courtesy Foakes' ton, the visitors got close to the 350-run mark. Perera was the star with the ball for Sri Lanka as he took a fifer. Sri Lanka in their first innings were poor with the bat. They had no answers to the spin trio of Moeen, Rashid and Leach. The offie was the tormentor-in-chief as he finished with a 4-fer. Angelo Mathews was the only Sri Lankan batsman who showed some fight. He scored a half ton but the hosts needed more from him.

England's session, England's day and one can probably say, it is England's match to lose now. They took the remaining wickets quickly post Tea and took a big lead of 139 and they have already added 38 to it. Their batsmen needed to battle out 12 overs today and their openers have done so without breaking a sweat.
The last ball has also been dealt with. Flighted ball on off, the batsman blocks it out. THAT WILL BE STUMPS ON DAY 2!
Penultimate ball negotiated, now one ball to go. Jennings defends it onto the ground.
On the stumps and it turns back in. The batsman gets right behind the line and blocks it out.
Slightly shorter and outside off, KJ guides it through point and the batsmen take two.
Loopy ball on off, the batsman prods forward and blocks it out.
On off, it is flatter, Jennings guides it towards point.
Slower through the air on the stumps, Burns keeps it out. So only an over left in the day.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot. They pick up a single.
On off, the batsman blocks it out.
BEATEN! Dananjaya has started off well here. He floats this on off, it pitches and then turns away. Jennings tries to keep it out but is beaten.
Tries to play the sweep shot but the ball hits the gloves and then the helmet. An appeal from the bowler but he is the only one doing so.
Tossed up on off, the batsman blocks it out.
Akila Dananjaya is back on. He was poor in the first innings and Sri Lanka would love a better show here.
Turning into off stump, Keaton gets completely beaten on this one.
Flighted delivery on off stump, Jennings cuts it towards third man. They pick up a single.
Floated on middle stump, Burns flicks it towards the leg side. The batsmen take a single.
FOUR! GREAT SHOT! Tossed up again on off stump, Rory dances down the track and hits it towards mid-wicket for a boundary.
Floated on middle stump, Rory defends off the front foot.
Tossed up on middle stump, Burns plays it off the back foot.
Flatter and quicker on the pads, the batsman works it towards square leg for a single.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Tossed up ball outside off, Burns makes a leave.
On the shorter side, KJ with the turn pushes it through covers for a run.
FOUR! Short and wide and put away! It was asking to be hit and Jennings puts it away through point for a boundary. The lead now is 166.
Flatter on off, the batsman blocks it out.
Flighted delivery on leg stump, Rory flicks it off his pads towards mid-wicket.
Tossed up again on middle stump, Burns defends from the back foot.
Floated on middle stump, Jennings sweeps it towards fine leg. The batsmen take a single.
Flighted delivery on leg stump, Jennings plays it towards the leg side.
Tossed up again on middle stump, Burns dances down the track and plays it towards mid-wicket. They take a single.
Tossed up on off stump, Burns defends off the front foot.
Rangana Herath is into the attack.
Tossed up on off, the batsman blocks it safely.
On the stumps this time, Keaton keeps it out.
Fires it on the pads, Jennings tries to defend but gets an inside edge onto his pads. The ball lobs away from short leg.
The batsman works it down the leg side.
On the shorter side outside off, Jennings pushes it to the man at covers.
This is flatter and on middle, the batsman blocks it out.
Back of a length delivery on middle stump, Keaton plays it off the back foot towards covers. They come back for two.
Length delivery outside off stump, Jennings lets it go.
Back of a length on middle stump, Burns plays it off the back foot. The batsmen take a single.
Length delivery on off stump, Rory pushes it to the off side.
On a good length on off stump, Burns plays it off the front foot. There is no movement for Lakmal.
Bowls on a good length, Burns defends off the front foot.
Flicked with the angle through mid-wicket for a couple.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
This is slightly fuller, Jennings still goes on the back foot to keep it out but gets his bat down in time.
Once again it is on the pads, Jennings fails to put it away and gets hit on it.
Shorter but quicker, kept out.
Fires it on the pads, it is worked towards deep square leg for a run.
FOUR! Beautiful shot. Short and wide outside off stump, Keaton places it towards third man for a boundary.
Length delivery on middle stump, Jennings defends off the back foot.
Length delivery on off stump, Keaton hits it towards covers. The batsmen get a couple.
Good length delivery outside off stump, Jennings leaves.
Length delivery outside off stump, Keaton lets it go.
On a good length, Jennings defends off the back foot.
Fires it on the pad, Burns misses the flick and is hit on the pads. A muted appeal follows but the umpire shakes his head.
The first ball that really turned! Floats it up outside off, Burns tries to force it through the off side but is beaten.
Shortish and outside off, the batter pushes it to covers.
Uses his feet but Perera shortens his length. Burns tries to flick but is hit on the pads.
Tosses it up on middle, no turn for the bowler. Burns keeps it out.
Sweeps and does it well, towards fine leg for a single.
Plays the cut shot this time but since there is a man in the deep, only a run results.
Wide again outside off, left alone.
Could have been the fourth but Jennings decides to leave this one.
Third cut shot in a row! None were off the middle though. On the shorter side outside off, Jennings chops it down towards point.
FOUR! If you slash you should slash hard. KJ does exactly that. Short and outside off, Jennings goes for the cut but the ball takes the top edge and goes down to the third man fence.
Starts off with a short ball outside off, the batsman tries to cut but gets a bottom edge towards point.
Suranga Lakmal to bowl from the other end.
Down the leg side, Jennings tries to flick but misses. The ball brushes the pads and goes fine down the leg side. A couple taken.
Gives it nice air and lands it on off, Jennings lunges and blocks it out.
Uses his feet and strokes it towards mid on for a run. England are underway in this innings.
Flatter and outside off, it stays a touch low. Burns tries to punch it through the off side but gets a bottom edge to covers.
Another loopy ball on off, it is kept out nicely.
Tosses it up around middle, it goes on with the arm. Burns keeps it out.
